question: How must an applicant translate a supporting document that is not in English or French?

claims.text: Supporting documents in a language other than English or French must be accompanied by an English or French translation stamped by a certified translator or accompanied by an affidavit if a certified translator is not available.
claims.quote: an English or French translation stamped by a [certified translator](https://www.canada.ca/en/services/immigration-citizenship/helpcentre/glossary.html#certified_translator) or accompanied by an [affidavit](https://www.canada.ca/en/services/immigration-citizenship/helpcentre/glossary.html#affidavit) from the person who completed the translation, if it is not possible to have the translation done by a certified translator

claims.text: The translation package must include a copy of the original source document used by the translator and the translation of all contents of the original document.
claims.quote: The translation package should include a copy the original source document that was used by the translator, and the translation of all contents of the original document in either English or French.

basis: The applicant submitted a certified translation document under case 25845c7d8474aa76eed215c0570a8af3 for Canadian Express Entry review.
